classification.difficultyReason: Use explicitly supplied diameters and cyclic right-angle information to obtain two right angles in each arrangement, sum adjacent angles for collinearity, then apply the taught converse of Thales. Five intermediate targets guide familiar theorem selection and short deductions.

content.prompt: The centres of the circles are O and P.

spec.description: Two circles intersect at B above and A below. Left circle has centre O and point S at upper left; S, O and A are collinear. Right circle has centre P and point T at upper right; A, P and T are collinear. Draw SA and AT. O, P and A have red point markers.
spec.answerVisibility: All original givens/point identities retained, no computed student values or added proof segments.

answer.worked: Join AB, BS and BT. SA is a diameter of the circle with centre O, so $\angle ABS=90^\circ$ by Thales. AT is a diameter of the circle with centre P, so $\angle ABT=90^\circ$.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Hence, prove that S, B and T are collinear.

answer.worked: BS and BT lie on opposite sides of BA in the given two-circle arrangement. Therefore $\angle SBT=\angle SBA+\angle ABT=180^\circ$, so S,B,T are collinear.

spec.description: Two circles intersect at B above and A below. Left circle has centre P, point C at upper left and N near the bottom. Right circle has centre O and D at upper right. N, A, O and D are collinear, in that order. Draw CN and ND; a right-angle square marks ∠CNA. P, O and A have red point markers.
spec.answerVisibility: All original givens/point identities retained, no computed student values or added proof segments.

answer.worked: Join AB, BC and BD. In cyclic ABCN, the angle at N is the given right angle, so its opposite angle $\angle ABC=180^\circ-90^\circ=90^\circ$. AD is a diameter of the circle with centre O, so $\angle ABD=90^\circ$ by Thales.

children.label: iv
children.prompt: Hence, prove that C, B and D are collinear.

answer.worked: BC and BD are on opposite sides of BA in the supplied arrangement. Thus $\angle CBD=\angle CBA+\angle ABD=180^\circ$, so C,B,D are collinear.

answer.short: The given $\angle ANC=90^\circ$ invokes the converse of Thales.
answer.worked: N lies on the left circle and the given angle ANC is right. By the converse of Thales, its opposite chord AC is a diameter of that circle.
